text:
Stonebeck's marks have not yet met the tape

Rating: underweight

The headline numbers invite complacency: one_year_return of +9.3% against a ytd_return of +1.0%, with drawdown sitting at +0.0%. Taken at face value, this looks like a portfolio that simply paused after a strong run. We read it differently. A reported_vs_public_gap of -8.5% is not noise; it is the accounting residue of marks that have not caught up to what public comparables are already telling us*. When listed comps rerate sharply and the private book reports a flat year, the gap does not close on its own — it waits, and waiting fragilities tend to compound rather than dissolve.

Calder & Root's position — that policy support resolves the stress and one should stay the course — leans on the same data we do, but reads policy_rate_now at 4.75% as a ceiling rather than a floor under continued strain. We would note that hy_spread_now_bps at 380bps is still wide by any recent standard, and cpi_now at 2.7% leaves the central bank little room to ease quickly should credit conditions deteriorate further. "Policy support resolves the stress" assumes the stress is fully priced. Our prior says marks lag reality, and a gap this size, sitting alongside a public rally the private book has not participated in, argues for caution rather than confidence.

Picture the chart: two lines starting together a year ago, the public line arcing upward through the rerating, the private line drifting flat, the space between them the exact width of the reported_vs_public_gap — a gap that has only widened as the newsflow describes public strength, not private confirmation.

The risk to our view: should the private marks simply be conservative and catch up smoothly as valuations are refreshed, the gap closes without incident and our caution proves excessive. We think this outcome is possible but not yet demonstrated, and we would rather watch the reconciliation than assume it.

*Footnote: comparables rerating sharply is itself the newsflow's phrase, not our embellishment.
